voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: The Pacific, nineteen ninety-one. When NOAA began listening on the Navy's submarine hydrophones, one sound was already there.
A long train of rising tones, each several seconds long. Loud enough to be recorded across the Pacific.
It became known as Upsweep. In the recordings it seems seasonal, peaking in spring and autumn.
Its source lies, roughly, in the remote South Pacific, between New Zealand and South America. Whales were an early guess, but the tone barely varies.
It lies near what may be undersea volcanic activity. More than thirty years on, NOAA calls its origin unresolved.
